Not part of the body

The valve on the old boiler stuck twice last winter, and both times it was the same washer. I replaced it with a brass one from the hardware shop on the corner, which cost less than the bus fare to get there.

What the plumber said

He looked at it for about a minute and told me the pipe had been fitted backwards in 1987. Nobody had noticed because the flow was strong enough to hide the fault until the pump began to wear out.

We turned the section round on a Saturday morning. It took three hours, two of them spent looking for a spanner that turned out to be in the car the whole time, under the passenger seat.

  • One brass washer, bought on the corner
  • One borrowed pipe cutter, returned the same day
